title: The Neuro-Cognitive Approach to Urban Planning: Wayfinding Behavior Analysis and its Effect on Urban Planning
research_question: How does urban environment navigation, influenced by urban design elements (street width, building geometry, landmarks, intersections, building height, green areas), affect people's wayfinding behavior, cognitive activity (EEG), and visual attention (eye-tracking)?

participants.description: 358 men and 354 women, aged 21 to 57 (M=34; SD=11.7), university graduates from Turkey. All were right-handed and did not consume alcohol before the experiment.
participants.recruitment: Not explicitly stated, but implies volunteers from a university setting.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A virtual city designed with six distinct regions (Orange-Zone: cafes/restaurants, max 15m height; Purple-Zone: shopping centers/skyscrapers >15m; Yellow-Zone: human-scale residential, max 7m height; Green-Zone: parks/recreation, green architecture dominant; Red-Zone: amorphous geometries, different textures/materials; Blue-Zone: industrial zone, factory architecture). The city included narrow and wide streets, landmarks, intersections, and buildings of varying heights and geometries.

measures.construct: Brain activity (alpha, beta, gamma, delta waves)
measures.instrument: Emotiv EEG Neuroheadset (14-channel raw EEG data from AF3, F7, F3, FC5, T7, P7, O1, O2, P8, T8, FC6, F4, F8, AF4 channels)
Custom-developed Eye-Tracking (ET) kit compatible with VR glasses (12 micro illuminators, 4 micro cameras)
Observation of navigation in VR environment

findings.mechanism: indicator of increased stress factors when people cannot find direction

findings.mechanism: increased demands for attention and alertness
findings.quote: low beta (13–19 Hz) activity increased in almost 84 percent of the participants, especially when walking on narrow streets compared to those walking on wide streets.

findings.mechanism: related to perception and organization of complex visual perception, anxiety and stress points
findings.quote: participants in the narrow streets showed an increase in alpha waves in the left occipital lobe.

findings.mechanism: difficulty getting out of narrow streets
findings.quote: Participants walking in the narrow streets were found to spend 43.87 percent more time than those walking in wide streets.
it has been determined that wayfinding behaviors in narrow streets have weakened
the highest number of gazes and fixations was recorded during navigation in wide streets
the highest number of gazes and fixations was recorded during navigation in wide streets

findings.mechanism: visual-perceptual processing, attention, object recognition
findings.quote: An increase in gamma bands was observed as the participants passed a landmark and/or saw a landmark.
for landmarks, there was a longer fixation time period

findings.mechanism: easier to identify, better remembered
findings.quote: Therefore, it is fair to say that landmarks in the urban environment are easier to identify.

findings.mechanism: mental relaxation, arousal, easier direction finding
findings.quote: most of the high alpha brainwave values were higher when participants walked in areas with amorphous geometry than they were in areas with buildings with normal geometry

findings.mechanism: participants more active or very mindful
findings.quote: most of the high beta mean values were higher when participants walked in the amorphous geometry areas than when they walked in the normal geometry city area
it is seen in Figure 9 that the walking routes of the participants walking in areas with amorphous geometry draw a very clear and stable route

findings.quote: eye movements were recorded quite slowly in most of the participants looking at structures with amorphous geometries

findings.mechanism: difficulty finding direction, continuous wandering
findings.quote: people spend more time in areas where there are higher structures and they cannot find their direction, wandering in the same area continuously.

findings.mechanism: increased emotional responses, attention, visual perception, relaxation
findings.quote: the alpha wave in the occipital lobe showed significant changes. Regarding the relative strength of alpha in the left hemisphere (O1), a significant difference was found between the high and the low building (0.12 ± 0.02 and 0.06 ± 0.01, p < 0.05).

findings.mechanism: increased emotional responses, attention, visual perception, relaxation
findings.quote: a significant difference was found between the high and the low building for the relative strength of alpha in the right hemisphere (O2) (0.11 ± 0.02 and 0.05 ± 0.01, p < 0.05).

findings.mechanism: related to direction finding
findings.quote: when looking at the ET data, it was determined that people look more in low building areas. Therefore, it is thought that people's ET metrics (for longer the first time) are related to direction finding.

findings.mechanism: relaxation in environment
findings.quote: it was thought that they could move freely in this area and find their way easily.

findings.mechanism: foliage reduces beta activity
findings.quote: This may explain the low beta level seen in the green field environment of our study, in participants wandering in the so-called green-zone, compared to the response to the absence of any vegetation in the so-called blue-zone, where there is almost no green cover.

findings.mechanism: associated with increases in alpha activity when viewing street scenes, familiar motor action
findings.quote: Alpha activities were observed intensely in people who see familiar chain cafes (Starbucks) and markets (migros), especially in the orange-zone area where cafes are dense, and especially among people with high heat map densities in these familiar areas.

findings.mechanism: low beta activity decreased
findings.quote: EEG data showed that low beta activity decreased in wide streets; therefore, stress factors are thought to decrease in such streets.

findings.mechanism: object recognition is provided
findings.quote: it was observed that the gamma band increased in the seconds when participants saw the landmark. In this case, it is thought that object recognition is provided, and so landmarks have a positive effect.

findings.mechanism: increase in alpha and beta power
findings.quote: Considering that the increase in alpha and beta power is a sign of mental relaxation, amorphous geometry can be considered important data.

findings.mechanism: stimulating like a landmark, positive effect
findings.quote: it is thought that amorphous geometry can be stimulating like a landmark, and can cause a positive effect for wayfinding.
The most important area for urban design is the green area, where people spend more time.
Conversely, they spend the least amount of time in industrial zones, and they are separated from this area.

mechanisms: Increased beta waves in narrow streets indicate increased stress factors when people cannot find direction.
Increased alpha waves in the left occipital lobe in narrow streets are related to the perception and organization of complex visual perception, and anxiety/stress points.
Gamma band increase when seeing landmarks is linked to visual-perceptual processing, attention, and object recognition.
Amorphous geometry buildings promote mental relaxation (increased alpha and beta power) and act as stimulating landmarks, facilitating wayfinding.
Low beta activity in green environments is explained by foliage reducing beta activity levels.
Increased alpha activity in familiar environments (e.g., cafes) is associated with relaxation and familiar motor action.
Low-facing buildings increase alpha waves, indicating increased emotional responses, attention, visual perception, and relaxation, which facilitates wayfinding.
moderators: time (beta wave mean values in amorphous geometry)
implementation_implications: Urban design should prioritize wide streets to reduce stress and facilitate wayfinding.
Landmarks are crucial design elements for direction finding and should be strategically located.
Amorphous geometry in buildings can serve as stimulating landmarks and positively affect wayfinding.
Intersections should be designed to help people remain alert and calm, potentially through clear signage or distinct features.
Low-rise buildings contribute to easier wayfinding and increased emotional comfort.
Creating green areas in city centers is important for well-being and encourages people to spend more time.
Industrial zones should be separated from city centers and positioned as far as possible.

limitations: External factors such as light, ambient sound, and ambient temperature were not controlled and can affect cognitive activity and EEG data.
The EEG device used had only 14 channels, limiting the clarity of brain activity analysis. Future research could use EEG or FMRI with more channels.
